US Launches Seventh Consecutive Night of Strikes on Iran

The United States military conducted its seventh consecutive night of strikes against Iran on July 17, 2026, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM). The operation began at 19:00 GMT and employed "fighter aircraft, aerial drones and warships" targeting Iran's "surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities."

Locations and Damage
CENTCOM identified targeted areas including Jask, Sirik, Bushehr, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Ahvaz, and Yazd. Iranian state media reported five explosions in Yazd and three in Sirik during early Saturday hours. At least three people were killed and eight wounded in attacks on Hormozgan province, bordering the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian Response and Escalation Warning
Major-General Mohsen Rezaei, advising Iran's supreme leader, cautioned that Tehran will transition to "offence and complete destruction" if American attacks persist. He stated Iran would resume "full-scale offensive operations" if strikes continue for another two or three days, adding that "Iran will no longer limit itself to retaliatory, like-for-like responses."

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and military claimed strikes against US assets in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait. Jordan's military reported intercepting ten Iranian missiles with no casualties or damage reported.

Regional Concerns
Kuwait announced Iranian strikes damaged electricity generation units at a power and water plant. The US State Department advised Americans to reconsider Middle East travel due to escalating regional tensions.
